title: In each fixed dimension at least three, every two-coloring of a sufficiently large Cartesian product of cliques contains a product of n-cliques monochromatic in every coordinate direction, with a doubly exponential bound in n^d
difficulty: After ordinary finite Ramsey bounds, elementary sampling estimates and pigeonholing, the remaining proof must construct a recursively consistent product and prove a separate density induction with quantitatively controlled loss in every dimension. The final synchronized coordinate extraction combines these two new constructions to keep the bound doubly exponential for each fixed dimension, exceeding ordinary qualification exercises in Ramsey theory; conservative H1.
